entries.input: In a group $G$, the inverse of a product $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ is $a_n^{-1} \cdots a_2^{-1} a_1^{-1}$.
entries.name: InverseOfListProduct
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (l : List G)
entries.conclusion: l.prod⁻¹ = (l.map fun a => a⁻¹).reverse.prod
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the empty list in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group and $a, b \in G$. The equation $a x = b$ has exactly one solution $x \in G$, and the equation $y a = b$ has exactly one solution $y \in G$.
entries.name: UniqueSolutionsOfGroupEquations
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G)
entries.conclusion: (∃! x : G, a * x = b) ∧ ∃! y : G, y * a = b
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $a = b = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of a group $G$. Then $x^2 = 1$ if and only if the order of $x$ is $1$ or $2$.
entries.name: SquareOneIffOrderOneOrTwo
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G)
entries.conclusion: x ^ 2 = 1 ↔ orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = 2
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x, y$ be elements of a group $G$. Then $xy = yx$ if and only if $y^{-1} x y = x$, if and only if $x^{-1} y^{-1} x y = 1$.
entries.name: CommuteIffConjugateFixes
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x y : G)
entries.conclusion: (x * y = y * x ↔ y⁻¹ * x * y = x) ∧ (x * y = y * x ↔ x⁻¹ * y⁻¹ * x * y = 1)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = y = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: In a group $G$, an element $x$ and its inverse $x^{-1}$ have the same order.
entries.name: OrderOfInverse
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G)
entries.conclusion: orderOf x⁻¹ = orderOf x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of odd (finite) order in a group $G$. Then $x = (x^2)^k$ for some natural number $k$.
entries.name: OddOrderElementIsPowerOfSquare
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G) (h : Odd (orderOf x))
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: In a group $G$, an element $x$ and any conjugate $g^{-1} x g$ have the same order; consequently $ab$ and $ba$ have the same order for all $a, b \in G$.
entries.name: OrderOfConjugateAndReversedProduct
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x g a b : G)
entries.conclusion: orderOf (g⁻¹ * x * g) = orderOf x ∧ orderOf (a * b) = orderOf (b * a)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: all four elements equal to $1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of a group $G$ of finite order $n = st$ with $s, t$ positive integers. Then $x^s$ has order $t$.
entries.name: OrderOfPowerWhenOrderFactors
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G) (s t : ℕ) (h : orderOf x = s * t) (h0 : 0 < s * t)
entries.conclusion: orderOf (x ^ s) = t
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$, $s = t = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $a, b$ be commuting elements of a group $G$. Then $(ab)^n = a^n b^n$ for every integer $n$.
entries.name: PowerOfCommutingProduct
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) (h : Commute a b) (n : ℤ)
entries.conclusion: (a * b) ^ n = a ^ n * b ^ n
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $a = b = 1$, $n = 0$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $A, B$ be groups. The direct product $A \times B$ is abelian if and only if both $A$ and $B$ are abelian.
entries.name: ProductAbelianIffFactorsAbelian
entries.binders: {A B : Type*} [Group A] [Group B]
entries.conclusion: (∀ x y : A × B, x * y = y * x) ↔ (∀ x y : A, x * y = y * x) ∧ ∀ x y : B, x * y = y * x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $A = B = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $A, B$ be groups, $a \in A$ and $b \in B$. The order of $(a, b)$ in $A \times B$ is the least common multiple of the orders of $a$ and $b$ (an element of infinite order has order $0$ in this convention).
entries.name: OrderInDirectProduct
entries.binders: {A B : Type*} [Group A] [Group B] (a : A) (b : B)
entries.conclusion: orderOf (a, b) = Nat.lcm (orderOf a) (orderOf b)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $a = b = 1$ in $A = B = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Every finite group of even order contains an element of order $2$.
entries.name: EvenOrderGroupHasInvolution
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (h : Even (Nat.card G))
entries.conclusion: ∃ x : G, orderOf x = 2
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of finite order $n$ in a group $G$. Then $1, x, x^2, \dots, x^{n-1}$ are pairwise distinct, and $n \le |G|$ when $G$ is finite.
entries.name: PowersBelowOrderDistinct
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (x : G)
entries.conclusion: Function.Injective (fun i : Fin (orderOf x) => x ^ (i : ℕ)) ∧ orderOf x ≤ Nat.card G
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of infinite order in a group $G$. Then the powers $x^n$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, are pairwise distinct.
entries.name: InfiniteOrderPowersDistinct
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G) (h : orderOf x = 0)
entries.conclusion: Function.Injective fun n : ℤ => x ^ n
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$ (written additively, the generator).

entries.input: In the dihedral group $D_{2n}$ of order $2n$ ($n \ge 1$), the basic rotation $r$ has order $n$.
entries.name: DihedralRotationOrder
entries.conclusion: orderOf (DihedralGroup.r (1 : ZMod n)) = n

entries.input: In the dihedral group $D_{2n}$ ($n \ge 1$), every element that is not a power of the rotation $r$ (that is, every reflection $s r^i$) has order $2$.
entries.name: DihedralReflectionsHaveOrderTwo
entries.binders: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (i : ZMod n)
entries.conclusion: orderOf (DihedralGroup.sr i) = 2

entries.input: In the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, every reflection $x = s r^i$ satisfies $r x = x r^{-1}$.
entries.name: DihedralRotationConjugatedByReflection
entries.binders: (n : ℕ) (i : ZMod n)
entries.conclusion: DihedralGroup.r 1 * DihedralGroup.sr i = DihedralGroup.sr i * (DihedralGroup.r 1)⁻¹

entries.input: Let $n = 2k$ with $k \ge 2$. The center of the dihedral group $D_{2n}$ consists exactly of $1$ and $r^k$.
entries.name: DihedralCenterEven
entries.binders: (n k : ℕ) (hn : n = 2 * k) (hk : 2 ≤ k)
entries.conclusion: (Subgroup.center (DihedralGroup n) : Set (DihedralGroup n)) = {1, DihedralGroup.r (k : ZMod n)}

entries.input: Let $n \ge 3$ be odd. The center of the dihedral group $D_{2n}$ is trivial.
entries.name: DihedralCenterOdd
entries.binders: (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h3 : 3 ≤ n)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.center (DihedralGroup n) = ⊥

entries.input: Let $x, y$ be elements of order $2$ in a group $G$ and $t = xy$. Then $t x = x t^{-1}$.
entries.name: TwoInvolutionsDihedralRelation
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x y : G) (hx : x ^ 2 = 1) (hy : y ^ 2 = 1)
entries.conclusion: (x * y) * x = x * (x * y)⁻¹
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = y = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group generated by two distinct elements $x, y$ of order $2$, and let $n$ be the order of $xy$. Then $G$ is isomorphic to the dihedral group $D_{2n}$.
entries.name: TwoInvolutionsGenerateDihedral
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (x y : G) (hx : orderOf x = 2) (hy : orderOf y = 2) (hxy : x ≠ y) (hgen : Subgroup.closure {x, y} = ⊤)
entries.conclusion: Nonempty (G ≃* DihedralGroup (orderOf (x * y)))

entries.input: An $m$-cycle in a symmetric group has order $m$.
entries.name: OrderOfCycle
entries.binders: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (hσ : σ.IsCycle)
entries.conclusion: orderOf σ = σ.support.card

entries.input: Let $\sigma$ be an $m$-cycle in a symmetric group and $i$ a natural number. Then $\sigma^i$ is again an $m$-cycle (a cycle with the same support) if and only if $i$ is relatively prime to $m$.
entries.name: CyclePowerIsCycleIffCoprime
entries.binders: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (hσ : σ.IsCycle) (i : ℕ)
entries.conclusion: ((σ ^ i).IsCycle ∧ (σ ^ i).support.card = σ.support.card) ↔ Nat.Coprime i σ.support.card
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the transposition $(1\,2)$ in $S_2$ with $i = 1$.

entries.input: Let $p$ be a prime. A permutation $\sigma$ in a symmetric group has order $p$ if and only if $\sigma \neq 1$ and every cycle in its cycle decomposition has length $p$.
entries.name: OrderPPermutationIffProductOfPCycles
entries.binders: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (σ : Equiv.Perm α)
entries.conclusion: orderOf σ = p ↔ σ ≠ 1 ∧ ∀ c ∈ σ.cycleFactorsFinset, c.support.card = p
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $p = 2$ and the transposition $(1\,2)$ in $S_2$.

entries.input: The previous characterisation fails for composite lengths: $S_5$ contains a permutation of order $6$ that is not a product of $6$-cycles.
entries.name: OrderSixNotProductOfSixCycles
entries.conclusion: ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 5), orderOf σ = 6 ∧ ¬ ∀ c ∈ σ.cycleFactorsFinset, c.support.card = 6
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is a closed existential.

entries.input: The order of a permutation of a finite set is the least common multiple of the lengths of the cycles in its cycle decomposition.
entries.name: OrderOfPermutationIsLcmOfCycleLengths
entries.binders: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (σ : Equiv.Perm α)
entries.conclusion: orderOf σ = σ.cycleType.lcm
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the identity of $S_1$.

entries.input: The orders of elements of $S_5$ are exactly $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$.
entries.name: ElementOrdersInS5
entries.binders: (n : ℕ)
entries.conclusion: (∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 5), orderOf σ = n) ↔ n ∈ ({1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} : Finset ℕ)

entries.input: Let $2 \le m \le n$. The number of $m$-cycles in $S_n$ is $n!/((n-m)!\, m)$.
entries.name: NumberOfMCycles
entries.binders: (n m : ℕ) (hm2 : 2 ≤ m) (hmn : m ≤ n)
entries.conclusion: Set.ncard {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | σ.IsCycle ∧ σ.support.card = m} * ((n - m).factorial * m) = n.factorial

entries.input: The symmetric group on the set of natural numbers is infinite.
entries.name: SymmetricGroupOfNaturalsInfinite
entries.conclusion: Infinite (Equiv.Perm ℕ)
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is closed.

entries.input: The square of any permutation of a finite set is an even permutation.
entries.name: SquareOfPermutationIsEven
entries.binders: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (σ : Equiv.Perm α)
entries.conclusion: Equiv.Perm.sign (σ * σ) = 1
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the identity of $S_1$.

entries.input: A permutation of a finite set is odd if and only if its cycle decomposition contains an odd number of cycles of even length.
entries.name: OddIffOddNumberOfEvenCycles
entries.binders: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (σ : Equiv.Perm α)
entries.conclusion: Equiv.Perm.sign σ = -1 ↔ Odd (σ.cycleType.filter Even).card
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the identity of $S_1$.

entries.conclusion: Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun i : Fin n => Equiv.swap (Fin.castSucc i) (Fin.succ i)) = (⊤ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 1))))

entries.name: SymmetricGroupGeneratedByTranspositionAndNCycle
entries.binders: (n : ℕ)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.closure {Equiv.swap (0 : Fin (n + 2)) 1, finRotate (n + 2)} = ⊤

entries.input: Let $p$ be a prime. Then $S_p$ is generated by any transposition together with any $p$-cycle.

entries.binders: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin p)) (hσ : σ.IsSwap) (hτ : τ.IsCycle ∧ τ.support.card = p)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.closure {σ, τ} = ⊤

entries.input: The alternating group on a finite set is generated by the $3$-cycles.

entries.binders: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm α | σ.IsThreeCycle} = alternatingGroup α
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: a one-point set $\alpha$.

entries.input: For $n \ge 3$ the alternating group $A_n$ contains a subgroup isomorphic to $S_{n-2}$.
entries.name: AlternatingContainsSymmetricOfDegreeNMinusTwo
entries.conclusion: ∃ H : Subgroup (alternatingGroup (Fin n)), Nonempty (H ≃* Equiv.Perm (Fin (n - 2)))

entries.input: For $n \ge 3$ the symmetric group $S_n$ has trivial center.
entries.name: CenterOfSymmetricGroupTrivial
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.center (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) = ⊥

entries.input: Two permutations of a finite set are conjugate in the symmetric group if and only if they have the same cycle type.
entries.name: ConjugateIffSameCycleType
entries.binders: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (σ τ : Equiv.Perm α)
entries.conclusion: IsConj σ τ ↔ σ.cycleType = τ.cycleType
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the identity of $S_1$, twice.

entries.input: The number of conjugacy classes of $S_n$ equals the number of partitions of $n$.
entries.name: ConjugacyClassesOfSymmetricGroupArePartitions
entries.binders: (n : ℕ)
entries.conclusion: Nat.card (ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) = Nat.card (Nat.Partition n)

entries.input: Let $n \ge 1$ and $\sigma$ an $n$-cycle in $S_n$. The conjugacy class of $\sigma$ has $(n-1)!$ elements and the centralizer of $\sigma$ is the cyclic group generated by $\sigma$.

entries.conclusion: Set.ncard {τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) | IsConj σ τ} = (n - 1).factorial ∧ Subgroup.centralizer {σ} = Subgroup.zpowers σ
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $n = 2$ and $\sigma = (1\,2)$.

entries.input: Let $n \ge 1$ and $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$. The stabilizer of $i$ in $S_n$ has order $(n-1)!$.

entries.binders: (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n)
entries.conclusion: Nat.card (MulAction.stabilizer (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) i) = (n - 1).factorial

entries.name: AlternatingGroupSimple
entries.conclusion: IsSimpleGroup (alternatingGroup (Fin n))

entries.name: SymmetricGroupNotSolvable

entries.name: NormalSubgroupsOfSymmetricGroup
entries.binders: (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) (N : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) [N.Normal]
entries.conclusion: N = ⊥ ∨ N = alternatingGroup (Fin n) ∨ N = ⊤
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $n = 5$ and $N = 1$.

entries.name: AlternatingNoSmallIndexSubgroup

entries.conclusion: n ≤ H.index

entries.input: For $n \ge 5$ the commutator subgroup of $S_n$ is $A_n$.
entries.name: CommutatorOfSymmetricGroup
entries.conclusion: commutator (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) = alternatingGroup (Fin n)

entries.name: SignIsUniqueHomomorphism
entries.conclusion: ∃! ε : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* ℤˣ, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), σ.IsSwap → ε σ = -1

entries.input: Let $F$ be a field and $n \ge 1$. The group $GL_n(F)$ is finite if and only if $F$ is finite.
entries.name: GeneralLinearFiniteIffFieldFinite

entries.conclusion: Finite (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F) ↔ Finite F
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $F = \mathbb{Q}$, $n = 1$.

entries.binders: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
entries.conclusion: Nat.card (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) (ZMod p)) = p ^ 4 - p ^ 3 - p ^ 2 + p

entries.conclusion: ∃ A B : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F, A * B ≠ B * A

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group. The map $g \mapsto g^{-1}$ is a homomorphism $G \to G$ if and only if $G$ is abelian; the same holds for $g \mapsto g^2$.

entries.conclusion: Function.Surjective (fun z : CommGroup.torsion ℂˣ => z ^ k) ∧ ¬ Function.Injective (fun z : CommGroup.torsion ℂˣ => z ^ k)

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group with an automorphism $\sigma$ such that $\sigma(g) = g$ only for $g = 1$ and $\sigma^2$ is the identity. Then $G$ is abelian.
entries.name: FixedPointFreeInvolutoryAutomorphismImpliesAbelian
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (σ : MulAut G) (h1 : ∀ g : G, σ g = g ↔ g = 1) (h2 : σ * σ = 1)

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group and $g \in G$. Conjugation $x \mapsto g x g^{-1}$ is an automorphism of $G$, and $g \mapsto (\text{conjugation by } g)$ is a homomorphism $G \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$ whose kernel is the center of $G$.
entries.name: ConjugationHomomorphismKernelIsCenter
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G]
entries.conclusion: (MulAut.conj : G →* MulAut G).ker = Subgroup.center G
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $G$ acting on $G$ by left multiplication, and $x \in G$. The orbit of $x$ has exactly $|H|$ elements (it is the right coset $Hx$).
entries.name: OrbitUnderSubgroupLeftMultiplication
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) (x : G)
entries.conclusion: Nat.card (MulAction.orbit H x) = Nat.card H

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group and $S$ a nonempty subset of $G$ such that $x y^{-1} \in S$ whenever $x, y \in S$. Then $S$ is a subgroup of $G$.
entries.name: SubgroupCriterion
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (S : Set G) (hne : S.Nonempty) (h : ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x * y⁻¹ ∈ S)
entries.conclusion: ∃ H : Subgroup G, (H : Set G) = S
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $S = \{0\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group and $S$ a nonempty finite subset of $G$ closed under multiplication. Then $S$ is a subgroup of $G$.
entries.name: FiniteSubsetClosedUnderMultiplicationIsSubgroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (S : Set G) (hne : S.Nonempty) (hfin : S.Finite) (h : ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x * y ∈ S)
entries.conclusion: ∃ H : Subgroup G, (H : Set G) = S
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $S = \{0\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group of order $n > 2$. Then $G$ has no subgroup of order $n - 1$.
entries.name: NoSubgroupOfOrderNMinusOne
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (h : 2 < Nat.card G) (H : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: Nat.card H ≠ Nat.card G - 1
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}/3$ and $H = 1$.

entries.input: In an abelian group $G$, the elements of finite order form a subgroup (the torsion subgroup).
entries.name: TorsionSubgroupOfAbelianGroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [CommGroup G]
entries.conclusion: ∃ H : Subgroup G, (H : Set G) = {x | 0 < orderOf x}
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: In a non-abelian group the elements of finite order need not form a subgroup: in the symmetric group on $\mathbb{Z}$ they do not.
entries.name: TorsionNotSubgroupInSymmetricGroupOfIntegers
entries.conclusion: ¬ ∃ H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm ℤ), (H : Set (Equiv.Perm ℤ)) = {σ | 0 < orderOf σ}
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is closed.

entries.input: Let $H, K$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $H \cup K$ is a subgroup of $G$ if and only if $H \subseteq K$ or $K \subseteq H$.
entries.name: UnionOfSubgroupsIsSubgroupIffNested
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: (∃ L : Subgroup G, (L : Set G) = (H : Set G) ∪ K) ↔ H ≤ K ∨ K ≤ H
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = K = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $H, K$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $H \cup K$ is a subgroup of $G$ if and only if $H \cap K = 1$.
entries.name: UnionOfSubgroupsIsSubgroupIffNestedTwin
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: (∃ L : Subgroup G, (L : Set G) = (H : Set G) ∪ K) ↔ H ⊓ K = ⊥
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: as for the target.
entries.rationale: Replaces nesting by trivial intersection; two distinct subgroups of order $2$ in the Klein four-group meet trivially but their union is not a subgroup.

entries.input: The intersection of any family of subgroups of a group $G$ is a subgroup of $G$.
entries.name: IntersectionOfSubgroupsIsSubgroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] {ι : Type*} (H : ι → Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: ∃ L : Subgroup G, (L : Set G) = ⋂ i, (H i : Set G)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the empty family in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $H$ be a subgroup of the additive group $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $1/x \in H$ for every nonzero $x \in H$. Then $H = 0$ or $H = \mathbb{Q}$.
entries.name: RationalSubgroupClosedUnderReciprocals
entries.binders: (H : AddSubgroup ℚ) (h : ∀ x ∈ H, x ≠ 0 → x⁻¹ ∈ H)
entries.witness: ⟨⊥, fun x hx h0 => (h0 (by simpa using hx)).elim, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $n \ge 3$. The set of elements $x$ of the dihedral group $D_{2n}$ with $x^2 = 1$ is not a subgroup.
entries.name: InvolutionsOfDihedralNotSubgroup
entries.conclusion: ¬ ∃ H : Subgroup (DihedralGroup n), (H : Set (DihedralGroup n)) = {x | x ^ 2 = 1}

entries.input: Let $H_0 \le H_1 \le H_2 \le \cdots$ be an ascending chain of subgroups of a group $G$. Then $\bigcup_i H_i$ is a subgroup of $G$.
entries.name: AscendingUnionOfSubgroupsIsSubgroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : ℕ → Subgroup G) (hmono : Monotone H)
entries.conclusion: ∃ L : Subgroup G, (L : Set G) = ⋃ i, (H i : Set G)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the constant chain $H_i = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group. The centralizer of the center $Z(G)$ is all of $G$; consequently so is the normalizer of $Z(G)$.
entries.name: CentralizerOfCenterIsWholeGroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G]
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.centralizer (Subgroup.center G : Set G) = ⊤ ∧ Subgroup.normalizer ((Subgroup.center G) : Set G) = ⊤
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $A \subseteq B$ be subsets of a group $G$. Then $C_G(B)$ is a subgroup of $C_G(A)$.
entries.name: CentralizerAntitone
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (A B : Set G) (h : A ⊆ B)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.centralizer B ≤ Subgroup.centralizer A
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $A = B = \emptyset$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $G$. Then $H \le N_G(H)$, and $H \le C_G(H)$ if and only if $H$ is abelian.
entries.name: SubgroupInNormalizerAndCentralizerIffAbelian
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: H ≤ Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G) ∧ (H ≤ Subgroup.centralizer (H : Set G) ↔ ∀ x ∈ H, ∀ y ∈ H, x * y = y * x)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $H$ be a subgroup of order $2$ of a group $G$. Then $N_G(H) = C_G(H)$; in particular if $H$ is normal then $H \le Z(G)$.
entries.name: NormalizerOfOrderTwoSubgroupIsCentralizer
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) (h : Nat.card H = 2)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G) = Subgroup.centralizer (H : Set G) ∧ (H.Normal → H ≤ Subgroup.center G)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $A$ be a subset of a group $G$. Then $Z(G) \le N_G(A)$.
entries.name: CenterNormalizesEverySubset
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (A : Set G)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.center G ≤ Subgroup.normalizer A
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $A = \emptyset$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of a group $G$. The cyclic subgroup $\langle x \rangle$ has order equal to the order of $x$ (both infinite together, recorded as $0$).
entries.name: OrderOfCyclicSubgroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G)
entries.conclusion: Nat.card (Subgroup.zpowers x) = orderOf x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of a group $G$ and $m, n$ integers with $x^m = 1$ and $x^n = 1$. Then $x^d = 1$ where $d = \gcd(m, n)$; in particular the order of $x$ divides every $m$ with $x^m = 1$.
entries.name: OrderDividesEveryRelation
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G) (m n : ℕ) (hm : x ^ m = 1) (hn : x ^ n = 1)
entries.conclusion: x ^ Nat.gcd m n = 1 ∧ orderOf x ∣ m
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$, $m = n = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Any two cyclic groups of the same order are isomorphic (infinite cyclic groups counted as having order $0$).
entries.name: CyclicGroupsOfSameOrderIsomorphic
entries.binders: {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] [IsCyclic G] [IsCyclic H] (h : Nat.card G = Nat.card H)
entries.conclusion: Nonempty (G ≃* H)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = H = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of a group $G$ and $a$ a nonzero natural number. If $x$ has finite order $n$ then $x^a$ has order $n/\gcd(n, a)$; if $x$ has infinite order so does $x^a$ (in the convention where infinite order is recorded as $0$, both cases read $|x^a| = |x| / \gcd(|x|, a)$).
entries.name: OrderOfPower
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G) (a : ℕ) (ha : a ≠ 0)
entries.conclusion: orderOf (x ^ a) = orderOf x / Nat.gcd (orderOf x) a
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$, $a = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of finite order $n$ in a group $G$ and $a$ a natural number. Then $x^a$ generates $\langle x \rangle$ if and only if $\gcd(a, n) = 1$; consequently $\langle x \rangle$ has exactly $\varphi(n)$ generators.
entries.name: GeneratorsOfFiniteCyclicGroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G) (hx : 0 < orderOf x) (a : ℕ)
entries.conclusion: (Subgroup.zpowers (x ^ a) = Subgroup.zpowers x ↔ Nat.Coprime a (orderOf x)) ∧ Set.ncard {y : G | Subgroup.zpowers y = Subgroup.zpowers x} = Nat.totient (orderOf x)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 1$, $a = 0$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x$ be an element of infinite order in a group $G$ and $a$ an integer. Then $x^a$ generates $\langle x \rangle$ if and only if $a = \pm 1$.
entries.name: GeneratorsOfInfiniteCyclicGroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : G) (hx : orderOf x = 0) (a : ℤ)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.zpowers (x ^ a) = Subgroup.zpowers x ↔ a = 1 ∨ a = -1
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x$ a generator of $G = \mathbb{Z}$ and $a = 1$.

entries.input: Every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic.
entries.name: SubgroupsOfCyclicGroupsAreCyclic
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [IsCyclic G] (H : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: IsCyclic H
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite cyclic group and $d$ a divisor of $|G|$. Then $G$ has exactly one subgroup of order $d$.
entries.name: FiniteCyclicUniqueSubgroupPerDivisor
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] [IsCyclic G] (d : ℕ) (hd : d ∣ Nat.card G)
entries.conclusion: ∃! H : Subgroup G, Nat.card H = d
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}/2$ and $d = 1$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group and $x \in G$ an element whose order equals $|G|$. Then $G = \langle x \rangle$.
entries.name: ElementOfFullOrderGenerates
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (x : G) (h : orderOf x = Nat.card G)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.zpowers x = ⊤

entries.input: The additive groups $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Q} \times \mathbb{Q}$ are not cyclic.
entries.name: ProductsOfIntegersNotCyclic
entries.conclusion: ¬ IsAddCyclic (ℤ × ℤ) ∧ ¬ IsAddCyclic (ZMod 2 × ℤ) ∧ ¬ IsAddCyclic (ℚ × ℚ)
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is closed.

entries.input: Let $x, y$ be commuting elements of finite orders $n, m$ in a group $G$. Then the order of $xy$ divides $\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)$.
entries.name: OrderOfCommutingProductDividesLcm
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x y : G) (h : Commute x y)
entries.conclusion: orderOf (x * y) ∣ Nat.lcm (orderOf x) (orderOf y)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = y = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $x, y$ be commuting elements of finite orders $n, m$ in a group $G$. Then the order of $xy$ equals $\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)$.
entries.name: OrderOfCommutingProductEqualsLcmTwin
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (x y : G) (h : Commute x y)
entries.conclusion: orderOf (x * y) = Nat.lcm (orderOf x) (orderOf y)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: as for the target.
entries.rationale: Upgrades divisibility to equality; $y = x^{-1}$ gives $xy = 1$ of order $1$.

entries.input: Let $H$ be a group, $n$ a natural number and $h \in H$ with $h^n = 1$. There is exactly one homomorphism from the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ (which is $\mathbb{Z}$ when $n = 0$) to $H$ sending the generator $1$ to $h$.

entries.binders: {H : Type*} [Group H] (n : ℕ) (h : H) (hh : h ^ n = 1)
entries.conclusion: ∃! φ : Multiplicative (ZMod n) →* H, φ (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) = h
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $n = 0$ and $h = 1$ in $H = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $p$ be a prime, $n$ a natural number and $x$ an element of a group $G$ with $x^{p^n} = 1$. Then the order of $x$ is $p^m$ for some $m \le n$.
entries.name: PrimePowerRelationGivesPrimePowerOrder
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (x : G) (h : x ^ p ^ n = 1)
entries.conclusion: ∃ m ≤ n, orderOf x = p ^ m

entries.input: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $n \ge 1$. In the multiplicative group $(\mathbb{Z}/p^n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ the class of $1 + p$ is a unit of order $p^{n-1}$.
entries.name: OnePlusPHasOrderPPower
entries.binders: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hodd : Odd p) (hn : 0 < n)
entries.conclusion: ∃ u : (ZMod (p ^ n))ˣ, (u : ZMod (p ^ n)) = 1 + p ∧ orderOf u = p ^ (n - 1)

entries.name: UnitsModPowerOfTwoNotCyclic
entries.conclusion: ¬ IsCyclic (ZMod (2 ^ n))ˣ

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group and $x \in G$. An element $g$ normalizes $\langle x \rangle$ if and only if $g x g^{-1} = x^a$ for some integer $a$.
entries.name: NormalizerOfCyclicSubgroup

entries.name: CoprimePowerMapSurjective
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (k : ℕ) (hk : Nat.Coprime k (Nat.card G))
entries.conclusion: Function.Surjective fun x : G => x ^ k

entries.input: The automorphism group of the cyclic group of order $n$ is isomorphic to the group of units $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$.
entries.name: AutomorphismsOfCyclicGroup
entries.binders: (n : ℕ)
entries.conclusion: Nonempty (MulAut (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) ≃* (ZMod n)ˣ)

entries.input: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $n \ge 1$. The automorphism group of the cyclic group of order $p^n$, that is $(\mathbb{Z}/p^n\mathbb{Z})^\times$, is cyclic of order $p^{n-1}(p-1)$.
entries.name: AutomorphismsOfCyclicPGroupCyclic
entries.binders: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hn : 0 < n)
entries.conclusion: IsCyclic (ZMod (p ^ n))ˣ ∧ Nat.card (ZMod (p ^ n))ˣ = p ^ (n - 1) * (p - 1)

entries.input: For $n \ge 3$ the automorphism group of the cyclic group of order $2^n$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2^{n-2}$; in particular it is not cyclic.
entries.name: AutomorphismsOfCyclicTwoGroup
entries.conclusion: Nonempty ((ZMod (2 ^ n))ˣ ≃* Multiplicative (ZMod 2) × Multiplicative (ZMod (2 ^ (n - 2))))

entries.input: Let $G$ be a cyclic group with generators $a$ and $b$. Then some automorphism of $G$ maps $a$ to $b$.
entries.name: AutomorphismCarryingGeneratorToGenerator
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) (ha : Subgroup.zpowers a = ⊤) (hb : Subgroup.zpowers b = ⊤)
entries.conclusion: ∃ σ : MulAut G, σ a = b
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $a = b = 1$ in the trivial group.

entries.input: Let $H$ be an abelian subgroup of a group $G$. Then the subgroup generated by $H$ and the center $Z(G)$ is abelian.
entries.name: JoinOfAbelianSubgroupAndCenterIsAbelian
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) (hH : ∀ x ∈ H, ∀ y ∈ H, x * y = y * x)
entries.conclusion: ∀ x ∈ H ⊔ Subgroup.center G, ∀ y ∈ H ⊔ Subgroup.center G, x * y = y * x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Any two distinct elements of order $2$ in $S_3$ generate $S_3$.
entries.name: TwoInvolutionsGenerateS3
entries.binders: (x y : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) (hx : orderOf x = 2) (hy : orderOf y = 2) (hxy : x ≠ y)
entries.conclusion: Subgroup.closure {x, y} = ⊤
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = (1\,2)$ and $y = (1\,3)$.

entries.input: Every finitely generated subgroup of the additive group $\mathbb{Q}$ is cyclic.
entries.name: FinitelyGeneratedSubgroupOfRationalsCyclic
entries.binders: (H : AddSubgroup ℚ) (h : H.FG)
entries.conclusion: IsAddCyclic H

entries.input: The additive group $\mathbb{Q}$ has a proper subgroup that is not cyclic.
entries.name: RationalsHaveNoncyclicProperSubgroup
entries.conclusion: ∃ H : AddSubgroup ℚ, H ≠ ⊤ ∧ ¬ IsAddCyclic H
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is a closed existential.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group and $H$ a proper subgroup. Then $H$ is contained in a maximal subgroup of $G$.
entries.name: ProperSubgroupContainedInMaximalFinite
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (H : Subgroup G) (hH : H ≠ ⊤)
entries.conclusion: ∃ M : Subgroup G, H ≤ M ∧ IsCoatom M
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Every nontrivial finitely generated group has a maximal subgroup.
entries.name: FinitelyGeneratedGroupHasMaximalSubgroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Group.FG G] [Nontrivial G]
entries.conclusion: ∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: The additive group $\mathbb{Q}$ has no maximal subgroups.
entries.name: RationalsHaveNoMaximalSubgroup
entries.conclusion: ¬ ∃ M : AddSubgroup ℚ, IsCoatom M
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is closed.

entries.input: No nontrivial finitely generated abelian group $A$ is divisible: some $a \in A$ and nonzero integer $k$ admit no $x$ with $k x = a$.
entries.name: FinitelyGeneratedAbelianNotDivisible
entries.binders: {A : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] [AddGroup.FG A] [Nontrivial A]
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $A = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: A quotient of a divisible abelian group $A$ by any subgroup is divisible; in particular $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ is divisible.
entries.name: QuotientOfDivisibleIsDivisible
entries.binders: {A : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] (hA : ∀ (a : A) (k : ℤ), k ≠ 0 → ∃ x : A, k • x = a) (B : AddSubgroup A)
entries.conclusion: ∀ (a : A ⧸ B) (k : ℤ), k ≠ 0 → ∃ x : A ⧸ B, k • x = a
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $A = \mathbb{Q}$ and $B = 0$.

entries.input: Let $N$ be a subgroup of a group $G$ and $u, v \in G$. The left cosets $uN$ and $vN$ coincide if and only if $v^{-1} u \in N$.
entries.name: LeftCosetsEqualIff
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) (u v : G)
entries.conclusion: (QuotientGroup.mk u : G ⧸ N) = QuotientGroup.mk v ↔ v⁻¹ * u ∈ N
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $N = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}$ and $u = v = 0$.

entries.input: A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is normal if and only if its normalizer is all of $G$.
entries.name: NormalIffNormalizerIsWholeGroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: N.Normal ↔ Subgroup.normalizer (N : Set G) = ⊤
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $N = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is normal if and only if it is the kernel of some homomorphism from $G$; concretely, if and only if it is the kernel of a homomorphism from $G$ to the symmetric group on the set $G/N$ of left cosets.
entries.name: NormalIffKernelOfHomomorphism
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: N.Normal ↔ ∃ φ : G →* Equiv.Perm (G ⧸ N), φ.ker = N
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $N = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of a group $G$ and $g \in G$. The order of $gN$ in $G/N$ is the least positive $n$ with $g^n \in N$ (and infinite, recorded as $0$, if there is no such $n$).
entries.name: OrderInQuotientGroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] (g : G)
entries.conclusion: orderOf (QuotientGroup.mk g : G ⧸ N) = sInf {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ g ^ n ∈ N}
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $N = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}$ and $g = 0$.

entries.input: In the additive group $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ every element has finite order, yet there are elements of arbitrarily large order.
entries.name: RationalsModIntegersTorsionUnbounded
entries.conclusion: (∀ x : ℚ ⧸ AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℚ), 0 < addOrderOf x) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ x : ℚ ⧸ AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℚ), n < addOrderOf x
entries.witness_note: There are no hypotheses to witness: the statement is closed.

entries.input: Let $N$ be a normal subgroup and $H$ any subgroup of a group $G$. Then $N \cap H$ is a normal subgroup of $H$; moreover the intersection of any family of normal subgroups of $G$ is normal in $G$.
entries.name: IntersectionsOfNormalSubgroups
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (N H : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] {ι : Type*} (K : ι → Subgroup G) (hK : ∀ i, (K i).Normal)
entries.conclusion: (N.subgroupOf H).Normal ∧ (⨅ i, K i).Normal
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $N = H = 1$ and the empty family in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $k \ge 1$ divide $n$. The dihedral group $D_{2n}$ has a surjective homomorphism onto $D_{2k}$ whose kernel is the subgroup generated by $r^k$; hence $D_{2n}/\langle r^k \rangle \cong D_{2k}$.
entries.name: DihedralQuotientByRotations
entries.binders: (n k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (hkn : k ∣ n)
entries.conclusion: ∃ φ : DihedralGroup n →* DihedralGroup k, Function.Surjective φ ∧ φ.ker = Subgroup.zpowers (DihedralGroup.r (k : ZMod n))

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group such that $G/Z(G)$ is cyclic. Then $G$ is abelian.
entries.name: CyclicCenterQuotientImpliesAbelian
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsCyclic (G ⧸ Subgroup.center G))
entries.conclusion: ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group such that $G/Z(G)$ is abelian. Then $G$ is abelian.
entries.name: AbelianCenterQuotientImpliesAbelianTwin
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : ∀ x y : G ⧸ Subgroup.center G, x * y = y * x)
entries.conclusion: ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: as for the target.
entries.rationale: Weakens cyclic to abelian; $Q_8/Z(Q_8)$ is the Klein four-group and $Q_8$ is not abelian.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a group and $H$ a normal subgroup. Then $G/H$ is abelian if and only if $H$ contains the commutator subgroup $G'$; in particular $G/G'$ is abelian and every homomorphism from $G$ to an abelian group kills $G'$.
entries.name: QuotientAbelianIffContainsCommutatorSubgroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) [H.Normal]
entries.conclusion: (∀ x y : G ⧸ H, x * y = y * x) ↔ commutator G ≤ H
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $H, K$ be normal subgroups of a group $G$ with $H \cap K = 1$. Then every element of $H$ commutes with every element of $K$.
entries.name: DisjointNormalSubgroupsCommute
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] [K.Normal] (h : H ⊓ K = ⊥) (x y : G) (hx : x ∈ H) (hy : y ∈ K)
entries.conclusion: x * y = y * x
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = K = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$, $x = y = 0$.

entries.input: Let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $G$. Then $|H| \cdot [G : H] = |G|$; in particular when $G$ is finite the order of $H$ divides the order of $G$. (Infinite cardinalities and indices are recorded as $0$.)
entries.name: Lagrange
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: Nat.card H * H.index = Nat.card G
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $K \le H$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $[G : K] = [G : H]\,[H : K]$ (infinite indices recorded as $0$).
entries.name: IndexMultiplicativeInTowers
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G) (h : K ≤ H)
entries.conclusion: K.index = H.index * (K.subgroupOf H).index
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $K = H = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group and $x \in G$. Then the order of $x$ divides $|G|$, and $x^{|G|} = 1$.
entries.name: OrderOfElementDividesOrderOfGroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (x : G)
entries.conclusion: orderOf x ∣ Nat.card G ∧ x ^ Nat.card G = 1
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $x = 0$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a prime dividing $|G|$. Then $G$ has an element of order $p$.
entries.name: CauchyTheoremForGroups
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h : p ∣ Nat.card G)
entries.conclusion: ∃ x : G, orderOf x = p
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}/2$ and $p = 2$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group and $d$ a divisor of $|G|$. Then $G$ has an element of order $d$.
entries.name: CauchyTwin
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (d : ℕ) (h : d ∣ Nat.card G)
entries.conclusion: ∃ x : G, orderOf x = d
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: as for the target.
entries.rationale: Drops primality of the divisor; the Klein four-group has no element of order $4$.

entries.input: Let $H, K$ be subgroups of a finite group $G$. Then $|HK| \cdot |H \cap K| = |H| \cdot |K|$, where $HK = \{hk : h \in H, k \in K\}$.
entries.name: ProductSetCardinality
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (H K : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: Nat.card (Set.image2 (fun a b : G => a * b) (H : Set G) (K : Set G)) * Nat.card ↥(H ⊓ K) = Nat.card H * Nat.card K
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = K = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $H, K$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $HK$ is a subgroup of $G$ if and only if $HK = KH$; in particular $HK$ is a subgroup whenever $H \le N_G(K)$.
entries.name: ProductSetIsSubgroupIffCommutes
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G)
entries.conclusion: ((∃ L : Subgroup G, (L : Set G) = Set.image2 (fun a b : G => a * b) (H : Set G) (K : Set G)) ↔ Set.image2 (fun a b : G => a * b) (H : Set G) (K : Set G) = Set.image2 (fun a b : G => a * b) (K : Set G) (H : Set G)) ∧ (H ≤ Subgroup.normalizer (K : Set G) → ∃ L : Subgroup G, (L : Set G) = Set.image2 (fun a b : G => a * b) (H : Set G) (K : Set G))
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = K = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $p, q$ be primes (not necessarily distinct) and $G$ a group of order $pq$. Then either $G$ is abelian or $Z(G) = 1$.
entries.name: OrderPQAbelianOrTrivialCenter
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (h : Nat.card G = p * q)
entries.conclusion: ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x ∨ Subgroup.center G = ⊥
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $G = \mathbb{Z}/4$ with $p = q = 2$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group and $H$ the only subgroup of $G$ of its order. Then $H$ is normal (indeed characteristic) in $G$.
entries.name: UniqueSubgroupOfGivenOrderIsNormal
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (H : Subgroup G) (h : ∀ K : Subgroup G, Nat.card K = Nat.card H → K = H)
entries.conclusion: H.Normal ∧ H.Characteristic
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $H, K$ be finite subgroups of a group $G$ of relatively prime orders. Then $H \cap K = 1$.
entries.name: CoprimeOrderSubgroupsIntersectTrivially
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (H K : Subgroup G) (h : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card H) (Nat.card K))
entries.conclusion: H ⊓ K = ⊥
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = K = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $H, K$ be subgroups of finite indices $m, n$ in a group $G$. Then $\operatorname{lcm}(m, n) \le [G : H \cap K] \le mn$; in particular $[G : H \cap K] = mn$ when $m, n$ are relatively prime.
entries.name: IndexOfIntersectionBounds
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G) (m n : ℕ) (hH : H.index = m) (hK : K.index = n) (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n)
entries.conclusion: Nat.lcm m n ≤ (H ⊓ K).index ∧ (H ⊓ K).index ≤ m * n
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = K = G = \mathbb{Z}$ with $m = n = 1$.

entries.input: $S_4$ has no normal subgroup of order $8$ and none of order $3$.
entries.name: S4NoNormalSubgroupOfOrderEightOrThree
entries.binders: (N : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin 4))) [N.Normal]
entries.conclusion: Nat.card N ≠ 8 ∧ Nat.card N ≠ 3
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $N = 1$.

entries.input: Let $G$ be a finite group, $N$ a normal subgroup and $H$ a subgroup with $|H|$ relatively prime to $[G : N]$. Then $H \le N$.
entries.name: CoprimeOrderForcesContainmentInNormalSubgroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (N H : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] (h : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card H) N.index)
entries.conclusion: H ≤ N
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $N = G = \mathbb{Z}/2$ and $H = 1$.

entries.input: Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of a finite group $G$ with $|N|$ relatively prime to $[G : N]$. Then $N$ is the only subgroup of $G$ of order $|N|$.
entries.name: NormalHallSubgroupUnique
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] (h : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card N) N.index) (K : Subgroup G) (hK : Nat.card K = Nat.card N)
entries.conclusion: K = N
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $N = K = G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: The additive group $\mathbb{Q}$ has no proper subgroup of finite index.
entries.name: RationalsNoProperFiniteIndexSubgroup
entries.binders: (H : AddSubgroup ℚ) (h : 0 < H.index)

entries.input: Let $H$ be a proper subgroup of a finite group $G$. Then $G$ is not the union of the conjugates of $H$.
entries.name: GroupNotUnionOfConjugatesOfProperSubgroup
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (H : Subgroup G) (hH : H ≠ ⊤)
entries.conclusion: ∃ g : G, ∀ x : G, g ∉ H.map (MulAut.conj x).toMonoidHom
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = 1 \le G = \mathbb{Z}/2$.

entries.input: Let $\varphi \colon G \to H$ be a homomorphism of groups. Then $\ker \varphi$ is normal in $G$ and $G/\ker \varphi$ is isomorphic to the image of $\varphi$; moreover $[G : \ker \varphi] = |\varphi(G)|$ and $\varphi$ is injective if and only if $\ker \varphi = 1$.
entries.name: FirstIsomorphismTheorem
entries.binders: {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (φ : G →* H)
entries.conclusion: Nonempty (G ⧸ φ.ker ≃* φ.range) ∧ φ.ker.index = Nat.card φ.range ∧ (Function.Injective φ ↔ φ.ker = ⊥)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: the trivial homomorphism $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $A, B$ be subgroups of a group $G$ with $B$ normal. Then $AB$ is a subgroup, $A \cap B$ is normal in $A$, and $A/(A \cap B) \cong AB/B$.
entries.name: SecondIsomorphismTheorem
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G) [B.Normal]
entries.conclusion: Nonempty (A ⧸ B.subgroupOf A ≃* ↥(A ⊔ B) ⧸ B.subgroupOf (A ⊔ B))
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $A = B = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $H \le K$ be normal subgroups of a group $G$. Then $K/H$ is normal in $G/H$ and $(G/H)/(K/H) \cong G/K$.
entries.name: ThirdIsomorphismTheorem
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] [K.Normal] (h : H ≤ K)
entries.conclusion: Nonempty ((G ⧸ H) ⧸ K.map (QuotientGroup.mk' H) ≃* G ⧸ K)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = K = 1$ in $G = \mathbb{Z}$.

entries.input: Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of a group $G$. The subgroups of $G$ containing $N$ correspond bijectively and order-preservingly to the subgroups of $G/N$, via $A \mapsto A/N$.
entries.name: LatticeIsomorphismTheorem
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal]
entries.conclusion: Nonempty ({H : Subgroup G // N ≤ H} ≃o Subgroup (G ⧸ N))

entries.conclusion: Nat.card (Sylow p G) ≡ 1 [MOD p] ∧ Nat.card (Sylow p G) = (Subgroup.normalizer ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G)).index ∧ Nat.card (Sylow p G) ∣ (P : Subgroup G).index

entries.rationale: Replaces the congruence $n_p \equiv 1 \pmod p$ by divisibility by $p$; a $p$-group has exactly one Sylow $p$-subgroup.

entries.input: Let $n \ge 2$. Every group of order $n$ is cyclic if and only if $n$ is squarefree and no prime factor $p$ of $n$ divides $q - 1$ for another prime factor $q$ of $n$.
entries.name: CyclicNumberCharacterisation
entries.conclusion: (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Nat.card G = n → IsCyclic G) ↔ (Squarefree n ∧ ∀ p q : ℕ, p.Prime → q.Prime → p ∣ n → q ∣ n → ¬ p ∣ q - 1)

entries.name: AllProperSubgroupsAbelianImpliesSolvable
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (h : ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → ∀ x ∈ H, ∀ y ∈ H, x * y = y * x)

entries.name: InternalDirectProductOfCommutingSubgroups
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G) (h1 : H ⊓ K = ⊥) (h2 : H ⊔ K = ⊤) (h3 : ∀ x ∈ H, ∀ y ∈ K, x * y = y * x)

entries.name: RecognisingSemidirectProducts
entries.binders: {G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] (h : H ⊓ K = ⊥)

entries.input: Let $H, K$ be groups and $\varphi \colon K \to \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ a homomorphism. The copy of $K$ inside $H \rtimes_\varphi K$ is normal if and only if $\varphi$ is trivial (in which case $H \rtimes_\varphi K$ is the direct product).

entries.conclusion: (SemidirectProduct.inr : K →* SemidirectProduct H K φ).range.Normal ↔ φ = 1

entries.input: Let $H$ be a group. In the holomorph $H \rtimes \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ every automorphism of $H$ is induced by conjugation by some element: for each $\sigma \in \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ there is $g$ with $g h g^{-1} = \sigma(h)$ for all $h \in H$ (identifying $H$ with its image).
entries.name: HolomorphRealisesAutomorphisms
entries.binders: {H : Type*} [Group H] (σ : MulAut H)
entries.conclusion: ∃ g : SemidirectProduct H (MulAut H) (MonoidHom.id (MulAut H)), ∀ h : H, g * SemidirectProduct.inl h * g⁻¹ = SemidirectProduct.inl (σ h)
entries.witness_note: The statement quantifies over a group type through implicit type binders and instance binders, which `∃` cannot close, so no witness of the checked shape exists. The hypotheses are satisfiable: $H = \mathbb{Z}$ with $\sigma$ the identity.
